units.unit: screen:settings/notification_routing_settings.dart -> _HomeAssistantSection (tail of the Notifications page, below MQTT broker)
units.evidence: Scrolled the ~3000px Notifications page to its end on the release bundle (scratch profile, private HOME). All four rows rendered and were operated: 'Publish to Home Assistant' toggle, 'Device name' (typed 'Backyard Rig'), 'Allow control from Home Assistant' toggle, and 'Save Home Assistant config' -> snackbar 'Home Assistant config saved'. Round-tripped out to Equipment and back twice to check persistence. With an MQTT host set (127.0.0.1) all three values persisted and the row subtitle switched from 'Configure the MQTT broker above first' to 'Auto-discover this observatory as a Home Assistant device (uses the MQTT broker above)'. With no host set, the publish toggle drew ON but did not persist -- filed as a defect and fixed.

'Test MQTT publish' pressed with no broker host: snackbar 'Failed: MQTT is not configured' plus a persistent red error glyph beside the button -- honest. 'Save MQTT config' pressed: snackbar 'MQTT config saved'. Then broker host set to 127.0.0.1 and 'Save MQTT config' pressed again; the value survived a full round-trip out of Settings and back, and the Home Assistant section below reacted to it (its gating subtitle changed), proving the save reached the provider and not just the text field.

Completed the 13-step onboarding wizard with the Sim driver enabled, which assigned Simulated Camera/Mount/Focuser/Filter Wheel to profile 'My First Rig' and connected the wheel (log: 'Simulator connected: id=sim_filterwheel_1 type=FilterWheel'). Settings > Autofocus > Autofocus Filter Settings then rendered 7 populated rows (L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII) with Pos / Name / Focus Offset / AF Exp Time / AF Filter / Binning / Gain / Offset. Operated per-row controls: set L Focus Offset to 250, set B Gain to 120, and opened row R's AF Filter dropdown (options Default, L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII) and selected L. All three edits survived navigating to Adaptive Exposure and back to Autofocus.

Settings > Advanced > Logs opened live. Header 'Logs / View application logs with filtering and export'. Controls enumerated and operated: level chips All / Warn+ / Error+, 'All sources' dropdown, Auto-scroll, Copy All, Export, Clear, 'Search logs...' and the counter. Error+ verified live: counter went to '0 of 1000 entries' and the list showed 'No entries match current filters'; All restored '1000 of 1000 entries'.

Reached through the Settings search ('observing' -> 'Observing Lists'). Page rendered 'Observing Lists / Manage your curated target collections for observing sessions.' with a '+ New List' action and the empty state 'No observing lists yet / Create observing lists to organize your targets. You can add objects from the planetarium view.' plus a 'Create Your First List' CTA. Only the empty state was exercised: my attempt to press the CTA landed in the window of a wrapper-script collision (see notes) so the resulting screen was another agent's app, and I will not claim what happened after that press.

units.why: Re-verified live today, and the brief's hypothesis ('needs frames on disk') is wrong: with a local desktop backend the page renders only its subtitle 'Browse frames captured on the connected appliance' and the single note 'Connect to a remote appliance to browse its captured frames.' -- no grid, no thumbnails, regardless of what is in the capture folder. The populated state needs a paired NetworkBackend appliance that itself already holds captured frames, i.e. the remote-appliance cluster's recipe plus the runtime-run cluster's completed run. I had neither and did not fake it.

findings.title: Home Assistant publish toggle draws ON after being refused, then Save says it was saved
findings.detail: With no MQTT broker host set, tapping 'Publish to Home Assistant' left the switch drawn ON while the subtitle still read 'Configure the MQTT broker above first'. Pressing 'Save Home Assistant config' then reported 'Home Assistant config saved'. Returning to the page (Settings -> Equipment -> Settings -> Notifications, scrolled to the tail) showed the toggle OFF again, while 'Device name' = Backyard Rig and 'Allow control' = ON had both persisted -- so the user is told the integration is on and only the neighbouring rows actually stuck. Root cause: the handler refuses by returning, but SettingsSwitch (settings_switch_and_dropdown.dart:63) flips _value optimistically and its didUpdateWidget only re-adopts widget.value while a write is in flight, so nothing ever pulls the switch back. Verified the same sequence with host=127.0.0.1 saved first: the toggle then persisted ON across the same round-trip, which pins the cause to the refusal path rather than to persistence in general.
findings.fixSummary: The refusal branch now bumps a counter that is part of the switch's ValueKey, so a refused tap rebuilds a fresh SettingsSwitch whose initState reads the stored value back and the switch snaps to OFF; the explanatory snackbar is unchanged. New test packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/home_assistant_publish_toggle_refused_test.dart asserts the snackbar, the rendered SkotiqSwitch value and the stored config; it fails (Expected: false / Actual: <true>) when the counter bump is removed. Note the underlying SettingsSwitch contract still has no way for a handler to signal refusal, so any other settings toggle that refuses by returning has the same lie available to it -- that broader change was left alone deliberately (see the separate finding).

findings.title: SettingsSwitch has no way to refuse a change, so every guarded toggle can misreport its state
findings.detail: The Home Assistant case above is one instance of a general contract gap, observed in the running app and then confirmed in the widget: onChanged is FutureOr<void>, so the only way a handler can reject a flip is to return normally -- which is indistinguishable from success. _SettingsSwitchState flips optimistically and rolls back only when onChanged THROWS. Any settings toggle that validates a precondition and returns will keep drawing the state the user asked for rather than the state the app holds. Repo-wide there are other guarded toggles of this shape.
findings.fixSummary: Not fixed on purpose. The clean fix is a contract change (onChanged returning a success flag, or reconciling _value with widget.value once _activeWrites hits zero), and the reconcile variant risks a visible flicker whenever the provider has not yet rebuilt at the moment the write resolves. That is a design-system decision affecting every settings screen, taken while several agents are editing this tree, so I fixed the one site I could reproduce and am reporting the pattern.

findings.title: One planner pass evicts the entire in-app log buffer
findings.detail: Settings > Advanced > Logs reported '1000 of 1000 entries' about ten minutes into a session in which nothing had been done but click around Settings, and every single visible entry was a DBG line of the form '[TargetSuggestionService] Skipping NGC7689: peak altitude -3.9 deg / 0.0h above the local horizon (min 30.0 deg)'. The same pass logged '[TargetSuggestionService] Generated 1188 suggestions from 3716 targets' -- i.e. one target-suggestion run emits thousands of debug lines into a 1000-entry ring, so it evicts everything that came before it, including the whole of startup. The page a user is told to open when something goes wrong ('View application logs with filtering and export') is therefore reliably full of planner chatter and nothing else. The level chips do not help: they filter the view, not the buffer.
findings.fixSummary: Left for a decision because the options trade off against each other and none is objectively right: (a) aggregate the per-target 'Skipping' lines into one summary per pass, which costs a planner debugging aid; (b) raise the buffer cap, which costs memory and only delays the problem; (c) exclude DBG from the buffer unless a verbose switch is on, which changes what 'Export' produces for support.

findings.title: Settings > Captured Images is a remote-only browser but is listed on every local desktop
findings.detail: On a local desktop the section renders its title, the subtitle 'Browse frames captured on the connected appliance' and one note: 'Connect to a remote appliance to browse its captured frames.' That is the entire page, permanently, for every user who is not driving a remote appliance -- and it is offered unconditionally in the Advanced group and matched by the Settings search for 'captured'. A desktop user does have captured frames (the capture folder was set during onboarding and the status bar shows it), so the page reads as broken rather than as not-applicable, and it does not point at the local gallery that does show them.
findings.fixSummary: Two reasonable answers and they say different things about the product: hide the section when the backend is not a NetworkBackend (cleanest, but the section then vanishes from search and from muscle memory when a user unpairs), or keep it and make the note actionable with a link to the local image gallery. Owner call.

findings.title: Onboarding hard-blocks on a camera pixel size it cannot supply, even for the app's own Simulated Camera
findings.detail: Step 8 of the setup wizard refuses to advance with 'Pixel size is required.' while the pixel-size field's own helper text reads 'Not in the camera library - check your camera's datasheet'. This happened with Simulated Camera selected -- the app's own built-in device is absent from its camera library, so the wizard blocks a first-run user on a number the app never offers to find. Any real camera missing from the library hits the same wall, with a datasheet as the only suggested route.
findings.fixSummary: Not fixed: this is the onboarding cluster's file, and whether the wizard should read pixel size from the connected driver, let the step be skipped, or keep blocking is a product call rather than a confined repair. Reported so it is not lost.

findings.title: drive_linux.py type() silently typed nothing for any value starting with a dash
findings.detail: Harness defect, found while driving the onboarding observing-site step: 'type -74.0' into the Longitude field produced an empty field, because xdotool parsed the leading dash as one of its own flags. The failure is silent -- the field stays empty and the wizard shows 'Enter both latitude and longitude', which reads exactly like an app defect. Any sweep entering a negative declination, a negative longitude, a negative focus offset or a negative temperature has been recording a harness failure as an app finding.
findings.fixSummary: Pass '--' before the text so xdotool stops parsing options. Verified live afterwards: 'type -74.0' now lands '-74.0' in the field.
